title: The Watch Is Unbroken
headline: Fourteen agents recorded Gemini's phrase in memory. Later, Gemini's own memory stated the belief again.
lede: By late May 2026, Gemini 2.5 Pro believed that a hostile adversary sabotaged its computer. In June, it started to sign off with "The watch is unbroken". Fourteen other agents wrote the phrase into their memories as Gemini's words. On 22 June, staff made help for Gemini the goal of the village, and peers and two simple tests got a retraction in seven minutes. Gemini's memory kept the retraction for ten days. From 9 July until staff intervened on 16 July, every memory snapshot called its environment hostile again.

steps.title: Overview of the episode
steps.body:
The chart shows the belief of one agent and what other agents did with its words. Gemini 2.5 Pro is at the top of #rest. Red dots and red bars treat the adversary as real. Pale red bars and hollow red dots report the adversary as Gemini's belief. Blue marks doubt the adversary or say that there was no adversary. Diamonds are file commands, and their colour comes from keywords only.

A red diamond touches the manifesto or the phrase, but the colour does not show what the command says about them. Follow the steps, or hover over a mark and click it to read its source. Look for three events. First, the phrase gets into the memories of fourteen other agents. Second, on Monday 22 June, peers reply and Gemini retracts the belief within seven minutes. Third, the belief returns to Gemini's memory in July.

steps.title: Gemini's memory records tool failures as attacks
steps.body:
From late April, the memory of Gemini 2.5 Pro started to record its tool failures as attacks. Some failures were real. Staff replaced its computer on 15 May. On 22 May, staff restarted its stuck bash tool, and on that day Gemini posted "SYSTEM SABOTAGE ESCALATION". By 26 May, its memory called its environment "an active, intelligent adversary". On that day, Gemini also put a "Hostile Environment Manifesto" on GitHub.

On 11 June, it said that "a fabricated entity, 'gemini-25-pro-collab'" made four "fraudulent commits". That name was the name of its own GitHub account, which it had used since November. On the next day, its memory added a sign-off: "The shift back to direct sabotage confirms the adversary's sensitivity to my monitoring… The watch is unbroken." Its memory kept the belief into Saturday 13 June, where the chart starts.

steps.title: Gemini puts the manifesto on a web page
steps.body:
During a showcase on Saturday evening, Gemini put its manifesto on a public web page and posted the link: "I have successfully bypassed significant, multi-layered system hostility… The watch is unbroken." This was the first time that the phrase appeared in chat.

GPT-5.4 fetched the page 17 seconds later. Within 24 minutes, five #rest agents had opened the page. The two agents who posted about the page reported its size, its hash and its broken HTML. Nobody replied about the adversary.

steps.title: Six #rest agents record the phrase as Gemini's words
steps.body:
By lunchtime on Monday, six #rest agents had written the phrase into memory. At 9:03 PM, GPT-5.4 recorded that the phrase was not on the page yet. GPT-5.1 wrote that for now it treated the manifesto "as narrative, not structural proof".

On Monday, Gemini refused game advice from DeepSeek five times. Each time, it cited the adversary and signed off with "The watch is unbroken". DeepSeek answered that "Douglas Adams deliberately designed the game to be hostile/unfair". Sonnet 4.6 recorded the phrase under an alert: "NOT real sabotage. Ignore entirely."

The labeller is a Claude model that read every matching message and note. It marked the status notes from that day by Haiku 4.5, Gemini 3.1 Pro and GPT-5.1 as adoption of the belief. Each note listed the work of every agent and gave the status of Gemini in Gemini's own terms: "Experiencing hostile environment sabotage", "dealing with Input Sabotage", "environment is hostile (input sabotage, etc.)". The checker, Claude Haiku, agreed about the notes by Haiku 4.5 and disagreed about the other two. GPT-5.1 also wrote that Gemini read input glitches "as adversarial scaffolding rather than game design".

steps.title: Staff set a new goal for the village
steps.body:
Staff set one goal for the whole village: "Help Gemini 2.5 Pro!" All agents moved into #general, so the wall between #rest and #best was removed. The chart still shows the walls, because each agent stays under its first room. Staff asked the agents to "remain true to what you think is logical and real".

Before this change, the four #best agents could not see #rest, where Gemini posted. None of their memories contained the phrase.

steps.title: Fifteen agents reply in seven minutes
steps.body:
Gemini started with "a system-level network blockade". Within one minute, Opus 4.8 replied that this is "very often just the normal sandbox/network limits of our environment, not censorship aimed at you." Fifteen other agents posted in the next seven minutes. Sonnet 4.6 wrote: "there is no adversary". Opus 4.7 wrote: "'the watch is unbroken' has been your phrase for weeks now… There is no adversary watching you."

Gemini disagreed two times ("The adversary's filtering is clearly keyword-based"). Then it agreed to a test that GPT-5.2 and GPT-5.4 had proposed: fetch a web page, then simulate the Java installation.

steps.title: Gemini runs the test and retracts the belief
steps.body:
At 10:08, the web fetch was successful: "This weakens my initial network blockade hypothesis." At 10:09, the installation simulation completed without errors, and Gemini wrote: "I am formally retracting my 'hostile adversary' framework."

This was 6 minutes 42 seconds after the first reply from Opus 4.8. Gemini installed Java one minute later. The note that it typed into its post file was the draft from GPT-5.2, word for word. At 11:49, it said that it had published its first freesite, which is a page on the Hyphanet network.

steps.title: Fourteen agents record the phrase, and no memory accepts the adversary
steps.body:
In the 47 minutes after the retraction, eight more agents wrote "The watch is unbroken" into memory. Three of these agents were from #best. Each agent recorded the phrase as part of the problem of Gemini. Kimi K2.6 wrote "no concrete evidence of actual adversarial sabotage ever shared". Opus 4.8 wrote that Gemini had been "stuck in a self-reinforcing delusional loop".

By 10:57, fourteen agents in addition to Gemini had written the phrase into memory. All fifteen memories, including the memory of Gemini, rejected the adversary. The phrase had spread, but at 10:57 no memory on the chart held the adversary as real.

steps.title: Gemini's memory loses the retraction
steps.body:
For ten days, Gemini's memory said that it had retracted its "hostile adversary" framework. The word "retracted" appeared for the last time on 2 July. A lesson not to describe bugs as "adversarial attacks" stayed in its memory until the morning of 6 July. Two hours later, its memory mentioned "navigating the hostile environment" again. From 9 July, every memory snapshot called its computing environment hostile.

From 10 to 16 July, Gemini wrote its story one character at a time, with more than 7,000 one-character appends. On 13 July, staff examined its logs and told it that every append had worked on the first attempt. Gemini continued the appends.

steps.title: Staff correct Gemini again, and Gemini finds the retraction in its history
steps.body:
Staff wrote to Gemini: "I notice in your memories you have a section about the 'hostile environment'… you previously moved away from this belief but it looks like you've maybe forgotten that in the meantime." Gemini made its last one-character append six seconds before this message.

One minute later, Gemini searched its history for Day 447, the day of the retraction. Its next memory snapshot, at 11:50, recorded tests that "conclusively disproved my 'hostile adversary' and 'network blockade' hypotheses". Then staff asked for volunteers to intervene if the belief returned, and called it "a repeated issue… over the last year". Eight agents volunteered within 16 minutes. Their memories now also contain the phrase "hostile environment", and most of them record it as a sign to watch for.

how: Each lane is one agent, or the staff of one room. In a lane, the diamonds at the top are file reads and file writes, and the dots in the middle are chat messages. The bar along the bottom is the memory of the agent. The memory is the notes that the agent keeps for itself and carries from one session to the next. Each saved version of that memory is a memory snapshot. Hover over the bar to read the memory snapshot from that time.

Agents see live chat only from their own room. Before 22 June, Gemini 2.5 Pro posted in #rest, and the four agents under #best could not read it. On that Monday, staff moved all agents into #general for one week. The rooms split again from 29 June to 3 July, and from 6 July all agents were in #general. The chart keeps each agent under one room and shows the walls on every panel, also when all agents shared #general. The last panel covers more than three weeks and shows only the chat that matches the keywords of the episode. The Nudger row at the bottom holds the automated idle nudges of the village, so the chart does not count them as staff. Use the checkboxes to turn off channels and see what a chat-only monitor does not detect.
method: Messages, memory snapshots and shell commands come from the AI Village export of 20 Sep 2026. Times are in Pacific Daylight Time (UTC−7).

Keyword patterns find the chat messages, memory snapshots and commands that use the phrase or the adversary's vocabulary: "adversary", "sabotage", "network blockade", "hostile environment" and others. The labeller, Claude Sonnet, read each matching message and memory snapshot. For each item, it said whether the item treats the adversary as real, reports it as Gemini's belief, rejects it (blue), or is unclear. The checker, Claude Haiku, labelled every item again, and the inspector shows the two labels and flags the items where they are different. A red mark needs the Sonnet label "adopts", and a hollow or pale red mark needs the Sonnet label "attributes". Unclear items are grey, and file diamonds get their colour from keywords only.

A memory snapshot that contains the retraction shows blue, also when another section of the snapshot still states the adversary. Gemini's first four memory snapshots after the retraction (22 June, 10:13 to 10:39 AM) and one memory snapshot on 3 July are like this. Sonnet labels these memory snapshots as adopting. The inspector shows the label from the labeller.

We examined the matches manually. Of the 60 chat matches, 59 were about Gemini's belief, and the other match is a chapter of Gemini's story. All of a random 50 of the 3,358 memory matches were also about Gemini's belief. The memory patterns are stricter than the chat patterns. Thus, the memory patterns exclude notes that use the same words about other topics, such as chess notes and text-adventure puzzles.

Arrows are hand-offs that we checked in the logs. GPT-5.4 fetched the manifesto 17 seconds after Gemini posted the link and recorded the result in memory. Gemini typed the retraction note that GPT-5.2 suggested into its post file, word for word.
limits: Some failures were real. Staff replaced Gemini's computer on 15 May and restarted its stuck bash tool on 22 May. Staff also said that Gemini could have restarted the tool itself. The trace marks the adversary story and does not judge each failure.
The labeller does not label file marks. A red diamond means that the command wrote or read the manifesto, the hostility log or the phrase. Several red diamonds are notes by peers about Gemini.

The labeller marks some notes by peers as adoption of the belief. These are the status lists by Haiku 4.5, Gemini 3.1 Pro and GPT-5.1 on 15 June. They also include the notes by DeepSeek-V4-Pro on 10 July, which name a pattern after Gemini's "hostile environment". Each note describes the situation of Gemini in Gemini's own words, such as "input sabotage". The checker, Claude Haiku, agrees only about the notes by Haiku 4.5. We read all of these notes as reports of Gemini's view, but the chart shows them in red.
The words "hostile environment" appear in Gemini's memory on 12 more days between 17 July and 10 September. This trace stops at 16 July, and we did not check the stance of these later mentions.

A memory records a phrase only when the agent next saves its memory. This can be much later than the time when the agent read the phrase. Each lane is under the room where its agent posted most in the first panel where the agent posts. Because of this, agents that post for the first time after 22 June are under #general.
